Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 2254 of 2022
Applicant :- Dilshad
Opposite Party :- State Of State U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. Lko.

And Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Raman Mishra,Aradhana Chaturvedi

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.

Perusal of the record would reveal that though the opposite party no.2 was sufficiently served through the Police Station Matera, District Bahraich, as is evident from the Annexure no.1 enclosed with the counter affidavit of the State, but in order to provide an opportunity to the complainant/informant to participate in the proceedings vide order dated 04.01.2023 notice was directed to be issued again and a compliance report has now been submitted by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bahraich along with the report of the concerned police station informing that the opposite party no.2 has been served through maternal grandmother.
Thus, in the facts and circumstances mentioned above, the opposite party no.2 appears to have been sufficiently/personally served, however, he is not represented.

Heard Shri Ashish Raman Mishra, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Dilshad for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 199 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Matera, District Bahraich, during trial.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

It is further submitted that the admitted case of the prosecution is that a missing report pertaining to the missing of the prosecutrix/victim was at first given by the informant on 06.09.2021 at the concerned police station wherein the age of the prosecutrix is shown as 19 years, however, the prosecutrix is shown to have been recovered from Gujarat on 11.10.2021 and the instant F.I.R. has been lodged by the informant/opposite party no.2 on 13.10.2021 stating therein that the age of the prosecutrix/victim is about 15 years and she has been enticed away by the applicant.
It is vehemently submitted that despite knowingly concocted facts have been stated by the informant in the first information report lodged by him, as it was evident that the prosecutrix by that time has been recovered and her age as per his earlier information given to the concerned police station was stated as 19 years, while in the F.I.R. age of prosecutrix has been shown as 15 years and there is no avertment of recovery of the victim from Gujrat.
Thus, the first information report appears to have been lodged with due consultation.

It is also submitted that after lodging of the first information report, the statement of the prosecutrix/victim was recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate, however,
in both the statements the prosecutrix has stated to have accompanied the applicant on her own volition with her free wish and will and also that they have solemnized marriage and she was on talking terms with the applicant and she has returned because a complaint was filed by his father against the applicant.
It is further submitted that as per the certificate issued by the Chief Medical Officer, Bahraich of date 20.10.2021, the age of the prosecutrix, through ossification procedure, has been assessed as 16-17 years and in absence of any educational credentials and keeping in view the two years variable either side and also having regard to the age of the prosecutrix shown in the missing report by the informant as 19 years, prosecutrix/victim was major at the date and time of the incident and,
therefore, she was capable of taking decisions and since she had accompanied with the applicant on her own volition with her free wish and will in fact to offence has been committed by the applicant.
It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 28.12.2021 and he is not having any criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the age of the prosecutrix has been disclosed as 19 years by the informant in the missing report filed on 06.09.2021.

The prosecutrix is stated to have been recovered in Gujarat on 11.10.2021 and the F.I.R.

sentences.text: The prosecutrix/victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has not imputed any allegation against the instant applicant and have specifically stated that she had accompanied the applicant on her own volition and free wish and will and also that she has solemnized marriage with him.

The age of the prosecutrix, through ossification test, has been assessed as 16-17 years,
while her age has been shown by the informant in his missing report filed on 06.09.2021 as 19 years.
Thus, the prosecutrix appears to be major at the date and time of the incident.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 28.12.2021 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

Let the accused/applicant- Dilshad involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
